interface.signature: def maxCandies(status: list[int], candies: list[int], keys: list[list[int]], containedBoxes: list[list[int]], initialBoxes: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.description: All input arrays have the same length n.

preconditions.expression: all(s in (0, 1) for s in status)
preconditions.description: Each status value is either 0 (closed) or 1 (open).

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= k < len(status) for k_list in keys for k in k_list)
preconditions.description: All key indices are valid box indices within the range [0, n).

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= b < len(status) for b_list in containedBoxes for b in b_list)
preconditions.description: All contained box indices are valid box indices within the range [0, n).

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= b < len(status) for b in initialBoxes)
preconditions.description: All initial box indices are valid box indices within the range [0, n).

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(k_list)) == len(k_list) for k_list in keys)
preconditions.description: All values in each keys[i] list are unique.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(b_list)) == len(b_list) for b_list in containedBoxes)
preconditions.description: All values in each containedBoxes[i] list are unique.

postconditions.expression: return_value == sum(candies[i] for i in accessible_boxes(status, candies, keys, containedBoxes, initialBoxes))
postconditions.description: The return value is the sum of candies from all boxes that can be opened and accessed starting from initialBoxes, following the rules of acquiring keys and contained boxes.
